implementation_notes: Rust spells both balking primitives as fallible non-blocking attempts: Mutex::try_lock() 'does not block' and returns Err(TryLockError::WouldBlock) - or Err(Poisoned) - where lock() would wait, and mpsc::SyncSender::try_send() returns Err(TrySendError::Full) when the bounded channel has no free slot. The check-and-return therefore becomes a match on the error, and the RAII guard keeps the bail-out path leak-free; for state-machine conditions the type system often removes the balk entirely, because typestate or newtype designs make the illegal state unrepresentable. Prefer blocking lock()/send() or an async channel when the caller must eventually proceed.
pitfalls: Folding every error into `_ => false` conflates WouldBlock with Poisoned; match TryLockError explicitly when a panicked owner must be distinguishable from ordinary contention.
std::sync::Mutex is not reentrant, so a nested try_lock returns WouldBlock rather than deadlocking - do not mistake it for contention from another thread.
Lock-free state transitions (atomic compare_exchange) need an explicit Ordering; Relaxed is easy to reach for and wrong once the flag publishes other data.
